corrected_value.authors: Gladwin, T. E., Figner, B., & Vink, M.
corrected_value.title: Anticipation-speciﬁc reliability and trial-to-trial carryover of anticipatory attentional bias for threat.

decision.location: Study 1 Discussion, lines 553-563; Introduction, lines 127-167; Study 1 Results, lines 367-376; References, lines 992-995
decision.quote:
The predicted within-subject eﬀects were found.
For Colour cues, attentional bias was drawn
towards the colour cue on which the target was presented in the previous trial. This replicated the previous ﬁnding on colour cues and carryover
(Gladwin & Figner, 2019). Carryover was also found
for negative facial expressions, as in previous
ﬁndings for threatening stimuli (Gladwin et al.,
2019; Gladwin & Figner, 2019). Importantly, this
eﬀect was asymmetric: a bias towards the negative
expression was found following target-on-negative
trials, but there was no reversal of the bias following
target-on-neutral trials.
decision.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. In the Introduction (lines 127-158) and Study 1 aims (lines 160-167), the authors review two prior studies reporting asymmetric trial-to-trial carryover for threat-related attentional bias—Gladwin & Figner (2019) on the dVPT and Gladwin, Figner, & Vink (2019) on anticipatory threat-related bias and trial-subset reliability—and set out to confirm and expand those carryover and split-half reliability findings using negative facial expressions. In the Study 1 Results (lines 367-376) and Discussion (lines 553-563), the authors directly compare their empirical carryover and reliability findings against both Gladwin & Figner (2019) and Gladwin et al. (2019). The sole shipped row (input_row_index 1514, 10.1016/j.actpsy.2019.04.006) is Gladwin & Figner (2019) in Acta Psychologica (coded at target_index 0), whereas Gladwin, Figner, & Vink (2019) (10.1080/20445911.2019.1659801) is a distinct published article in Journal of Cognitive Psychology with different experimental data and authorship that is absent from the shipped rows.

corrected_value.authors: Fang, F., Kersten, D., & Murray, S. O.
corrected_value.title: Perceptual grouping and inverse fMRI activity patterns in human visual cortex.

decision.location: Discussion, lines 886-891; Introduction, lines 212-228; Results, lines 612-657; References, lines 993-997
decision.quote:
It is perhaps not surprising that our study replicates the
reduction found in Murray and colleagues’ previous
work, given that we explicitly set out to replicate the
parameters used in the study of Fang et al. Clearly,
future work will be required to pin down exactly what
conditions are required for cases of perceptual grouping to lead to reductions in primary visual activation.
decision.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. De-Wit et al. (2012) explicitly replicate the stimulus parameters of Fang, Kersten, & Murray (2008) (10.1167/8.7.2) and empirically retest Fang et al.'s specific published findings: (1) that V1 fMRI signal reduction during perceptual grouping of a bistable diamond is restricted to the retinotopic representation of the stimulus and absent in adjacent retinotopic regions (Introduction, lines 212-228; Discussion, lines 681-690), and (2) that perceptual grouping produces an inverse activation increase in higher-level shape-selective cortex LOC/LO (Results, lines 612-633). The only shipped row (input_row_index 2262, 10.1073/pnas.192579399) is Murray et al. (2002) in PNAS, an earlier study by a different author team that preceded Fang et al. (2008) in Journal of Vision by six years. Fang et al. (2008) is therefore a distinct, genuinely absent original study.

decision.quote: The current study sought to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial by adding data from five additional cohorts ( N =270) as well as examine moderating effects. The study first examined FHF’s effects on key mental health outcomes: a multi-informant (child, caregiver, teacher) index of mental health problems, youth-reported posttraumatic stress symptoms (including dissociation), youth-reported quality of life, and caregiver- and youth-reported use of mental health treatment (including psychotropic medications).
decision.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Although the replication paper cites Taussig & Culhane (2010) (10.1001/archpediatrics.2010.124) for the main mental health findings of the Fostering Healthy Futures (FHF) pilot RCT on preadolescent youth in out-of-home care, the Method section establishes that there was only one prior FHF RCT on preadolescent youth in out-of-home care (the 5-cohort pilot trial recruited from 2002 to 2006, N = 156) before the 5 additional efficacy cohorts were combined in the current paper. Shipped row input_row_index 754 (10.1037/e522512014-027, Taussig, 2012, 'Fostering Healthy Futures: A Randomized Controlled Trial of an Intervention for Preadolescent Youth in Out-of-Home Care') is an alternate APA PsycEXTRA conference/grey-literature report of that same FHF pilot RCT. Because a conference/grey-literature record and full journal article represent the same original work, target_index 0 is already covered by shipped row 754.

corrected_value.title: The moderating effect of risk exposure on an efficacious intervention for maltreated children.

decision.location: Introduction, Current Study, Results (Moderating Analyses), Discussion, and References, line 1
decision.quote: In the FHF pilot study we found that (1) severity of neglect did not moderate outcomes, suggesting that children with severe neglect histories were just as likely to benefit from the intervention as those with less severe neglect histories ( Taussig, Culhane, Garrido, Knudtson, & Petrenko, 2013 ) but that (2) level of risk (i.e., exposure to ACEs) did moderate some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress and dissociative symptoms), such that maltreated children exposed to a relatively higher number of ACEs did not experience the same reduction in trauma symptoms as children exposed to fewer adversities ( Weiler & Taussig, 2017 ).
decision.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Weiler & Taussig (2017) (10.1080/15374416.2017.1295379, Journal of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology) is a distinct 2017 study reporting that baseline exposure to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) moderated FHF intervention effects on trauma symptoms such that youth with fewer ACEs experienced stronger reductions in posttraumatic stress symptoms. In the Current Study section, the authors formulate their sole directional a priori moderation hypothesis specifically to retest this finding; in Moderating Analyses they test the ACEs x treatment interaction on T2 outcomes; and in Discussion they explicitly state that their results 'replicated our earlier finding that children exposed to relatively fewer ACEs tended to benefit more on some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress symptoms and quality of life)'. Shipped row 754 (Taussig, 2012, 10.1037/e522512014-027) and target_index 0 (Taussig & Culhane, 2010) predated this 2017 moderation study by 5 to 7 years and reported main RCT effects rather than the Weiler & Taussig (2017) ACEs moderation finding.

decision.quote:
I tested the processing of two majority quantifiers in Bulgarian (Bg) and Polish (Pl): the
counterpart of English most (povečeto in Bg, większość in Pl, henceforth Most1) and a closely
related quantifier with the meaning of “the largest subset” (naj-mnogo in Bg, najwięcej in Pl,
henceforth Most2). I obtained three notable results:
• Most1 is verified by a Subtraction strategy as in (2) and not (3), directly replicating the
findings of Lidz et al. for Slavic;
• Most2 is verified by a Selection strategy as in (4) in accordance with its lexical semantics;
• the canonical verification strategies are used even in cases where either strategy would yield
the correct truth value.
decision.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Throughout the paper (lines 4-7, 25-26, 36-43, 131-132), the author explicitly identifies Lidz, Pietroski, Hunter, & Halberda (2011) (already captured by shipped row input_row_index 2248, 10.1007/s11050-010-9062-6, and coded at target_index 2) as the study whose 200ms dot-display visual verification paradigm and subtraction finding are directly replicated. Pietroski, Lidz, Hunter, & Halberda (2008) is an earlier paper by the exact same four-author team in the same research chain and is never mentioned anywhere in the Introduction, Methods, or Results; its only appearance is in a single concluding sentence (lines 185-186) grouping 'Pietroski et al. (2008), Hackl (2009), Lidz et al. (2011)'. Under the codebook replication-chain rule and review instructions, no distinct empirical finding from Pietroski et al. (2008) is independently retested beyond Lidz et al. (2011) (shipped row 2248).

decision.quote:
On two-color screens, where Most1 and Most2 are either both true or both false, the verification
procedure depends on the lexical item used. The patterns of accuracy for Most1 and Most2 are
conspicuously different (and have the same direction in both Bulgarian and Polish) indicating
that computationally Most1 and Most2 are different.
My results confirm and extend the findings of Pietroski et al. (2008), Hackl (2009), Lidz et al.
(2011) and indicate that semantics provides inviolable instructions to visual cognition processes.
decision.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Hackl (2009) ('On the grammar and processing of proportional quantifiers: most versus more than half') is never mentioned, described, or operationalized in the Introduction, Methods, or Results of Tomaszewicz (2012), which solely tests Bulgarian and Polish counterparts of 'most' (Most1) and 'the largest subset' (Most2) in the 200ms colored-dot visual verification paradigm of Lidz et al. (2011) (shipped row input_row_index 2248). Hackl (2009) is cited only once in the final theoretical conclusion sentence (lines 185-186) as supporting the general claim that semantics interfaces with verification processes. Because no specific empirical finding of Hackl (2009) is retested, it is not a missing original study, and the paper's actual replication target is already represented by shipped row 2248.
